{"ok": true, "tool": "load_skill", "data": {"name": "index_excerpts", "description": "Store useful excerpts of organized documents in Elasticsearch through MCP and search them - choose exact line ranges, build metadata, upsert without duplicates, verify with search, and sync current_path after a file move. Use for "положи/сохрани в Elastic", "проиндексируй", "найди в Elastic", "синхронизируй индекс".", "instructions": "# index_excerpts — procedure

## 1. Select documents
- Resolve the request to catalogued documents: `catalog_view(folder=...)` or `catalog_view()`; for "this file" use the document discussed earlier.
- Only documents in data/ with a document_id can be indexed. Empty documents (`is_empty=true`) are skipped with an explanation.

## 2. Choose excerpts by content
- `read(path, numbered=true)` to see line numbers.
- Pick 1-4 informative fragments per document (definitions, decisions, facts, steps). Each fragment is a contiguous 1-based inclusive line range, at most 60 lines, not blank. For a very short file one range may cover the whole text.
- Optionally write a short `summary` per range (it does NOT replace the text).

## 3. Build exact records
- `build_excerpts(document_id, ranges=[{start_line, end_line, summary}, ...])`.
- The tool copies the exact text, content_hash, title, category, current_path and computes the stable `excerpt_id`. Never edit the returned text.
- Re-indexing an unchanged document: `build_excerpts(document_id)` WITHOUT ranges reuses the ranges already stored -> same excerpt_ids -> no duplicates.

## 4. Write through MCP
- `upsert_excerpts(excerpts=<records from build_excerpts>)` (default mode="replace" keeps exactly this set for the document; use mode="merge" only to ADD excerpts to an already indexed document).
- Check the result: `ok=true`, `created`/`updated` counts, per-document `count`. A second run of the same version must show `created=0`.
- `ok=false` (es_unavailable, mcp_unavailable, excerpt_validation_failed): report the failure, do NOT say it was indexed. The catalog marks the document `error`. For validation failures rebuild with build_excerpts.

## 5. Keep paths consistent after moves
- When `move` returns `action_required`, or `catalog_view(status="pending_sync")` lists documents: call `update_document_path(document_id, new_path=<catalog current_path>)` for each (the server sets `category` from the `data/<category>/` folder of the new path). On success - path and category in the index equal the catalog - the catalog switches back to `indexed`; otherwise it stays `pending_sync` - tell the user and retry later.

## 6. Search and verify
- `search_excerpts(query, size=5..10, category=?, path_prefix=?)`. Formulate a lexical query with key terms (Russian morphology is handled by the index analyzer).
- Answer with: excerpt text (quote), `current_path`, lines `start_line-end_line`, `document_id`. If asked, open the source with `read(current_path)` and point to the lines.
- After writing, run one search for a key term of a written excerpt to verify it is findable.
- `get_document_excerpts(document_id)` / `index_stats()` show what is stored (useful to prove "no duplicates")."}}

{"ok": true, "tool": "load_skill", "data": {"name": "organize_files", "description": "Organize files from input/ into topic folders in data/ - inspect contents, choose or apply a folder structure, resolve ambiguous documents and name conflicts, move files and keep the catalog up to date. Use for "разложи/разбери файлы", "перенеси файл", "что лежит в папке", new files in input.", "instructions": "# organize_files — procedure

## 1. Inspect the current state (always fresh)
1. `ls input` and `ls` every subfolder of input recursively. Earlier listings are stale: the user may have added files during the session.
2. `ls data` (and its folders) to see the existing structure; `catalog_view` to see catalogued documents.
3. Only files still in input/ need organizing. Never copy or re-create files that are already in data/.

## 2. Read contents
- For each file in input/: `read` it (or `head` with n=40 for long files). Classify by CONTENT, not by name.
- Size 0 bytes -> empty file: do not read further; plan `data/_unsorted/`.

## 3. Choose the structure
- If the user named folders, use them exactly.
- Otherwise derive 3+ topics from contents; short lowercase English folder names, e.g. `courses`, `projects`, `meetings`, `howto`. Reuse existing data/ folders when they fit.
- Ambiguous document (fits 2+ topics): either ask the user ONE clarifying question before moving it, or choose the dominant topic and state the reason. Record the rationale: `catalog_update(document_id, note="ambiguous: ... chose X because ...")`.

## 4. Move
- `move(source="input/...", destination="data/<topic>/<file>")`, one call per file.
- `name_conflict` -> never overwrite. Use `suggested_name` (e.g. `notes_2.md`) or a descriptive name derived from the content (e.g. `notes_team_sync.md`), then retry.
- `duplicate_of` warning -> report it to the user; do not delete anything.
- If the move result contains `action_required` (document already indexed) -> call MCP `update_document_path(document_id, new_path)` right away (see skill index_excerpts §5).
- Moving between data folders works the same way: `move("data/a/x.md", "data/b/x.md")`. document_id and content stay the same.

## 5. Describe
- For each moved document: `catalog_update(document_id, title=..., description="1 sentence about the content")`.
- Optionally `write("data/<topic>/_about.md", ...)` with a short folder description (new artifact, not a document copy).

## 6. Report
- Table/list: old path -> new path, topic, one-line reason. Mention empty files, ambiguity decisions, conflicts and duplicates.
- To answer "what is in folder X": `ls data/X` (shows titles/descriptions from the catalog) and summarize."}}
